title: Greek Chicken Bowls

steps.text: Season chicken with olive oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Roast chicken at 425°F until cooked through, about 18 minutes.
Serve over rice with cucumber, tomatoes, and tzatziki.

storageNotes: Store components separately up to 4 days.
reheatNotes: Reheat chicken and rice; keep vegetables and sauce cold.
prepAheadNotes: Cook rice and chop vegetables up to 2 days ahead.
toddlerTip: Serve deconstructed with sauce on the side.
glucoseTip: Use extra vegetables and a smaller rice portion.

title: Turkey Kofta Plates

steps.text: Mix turkey with parsley, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Shape into small patties and sear until browned and cooked through.
Serve with pita, romaine, and yogurt sauce if desired.

storageNotes: Cooked kofta keeps up to 4 days refrigerated.
prepAheadNotes: Shape kofta the night before and refrigerate covered.
toddlerTip: Cut kofta into small strips and serve pita separately.
glucoseTip: Use lettuce as the base and half a pita.

title: Chickpea Greek Salad Lunch Boxes

steps.text: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Toss chickpeas, vegetables, feta, and olives with dressing.
Pack into lunch containers and keep cold.

storageNotes: Keeps 3 days refrigerated.
prepAheadNotes: Dress just before packing if you want the vegetables extra crisp.
toddlerTip: Serve chickpeas lightly mashed with cucumber sticks.
glucoseTip: Add grilled chicken or tuna for more protein.

title: Egg Muffins with Spinach and Feta

steps.text: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, pepper, and dill.
Divide spinach and feta among greased muffin cups.
Pour egg mixture over top and bake at 350°F until set, about 18 minutes.

storageNotes: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months.
reheatNotes: Microwave 20-30 seconds from refrigerated.
prepAheadNotes: Bake once for grab-and-go breakfasts.
toddlerTip: Cut into strips and serve with fruit.
glucoseTip: Pair with berries instead of toast for lower carbs.

title: Salmon with Lemon Dill Yogurt and Green Beans

steps.text: Place salmon and green beans on a sheet pan; season with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast at 400°F until salmon flakes easily, about 12-15 minutes.
Mix yogurt with lemon and dill; spoon over salmon.

storageNotes: Best eaten within 2 days.
reheatNotes: Reheat gently or eat salmon cold over salad.
prepAheadNotes: Mix yogurt sauce up to 3 days ahead.
toddlerTip: Flake salmon carefully and check for bones.
glucoseTip: Add a small roasted potato if needed; otherwise keep it vegetable-forward.

title: White Bean Tuna Toasts

steps.text: Mash half the beans with lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Fold in tuna, remaining beans, and capers.
Serve on toast with arugula.

storageNotes: Tuna-bean mixture keeps 2 days refrigerated.
prepAheadNotes: Make the tuna-bean mixture ahead; toast bread before serving.
toddlerTip: Serve tuna-bean mash with crackers or cucumber rounds.
glucoseTip: Use one toast and extra arugula or cucumber.

title: Lentil Vegetable Soup

steps.text: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in olive oil until softened.
Add lentils, tomatoes, broth, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer until lentils are tender, about 35 minutes.

storageNotes: Keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes well.
reheatNotes: Reheat with a splash of broth or water.
prepAheadNotes: Chop the vegetables ahead or cook the full soup for batch lunches.
toddlerTip: Blend a portion for a smoother texture.
glucoseTip: Pair with salad and keep bread portions modest.

title: Chicken Shawarma Sheet Pan Dinner

steps.text: Toss chicken with olive oil, lemon, garlic, shawarma spices, salt, and pepper.
Spread chicken, onion, and peppers on a sheet pan.
Roast at 425°F until chicken is browned and cooked through, about 25 minutes.

storageNotes: Keeps 4 days refrigerated.
reheatNotes: Reheat in skillet or microwave; add yogurt sauce after warming.
prepAheadNotes: Marinate chicken up to 24 hours ahead.
toddlerTip: Use mild spice and serve chicken with pita or rice.
glucoseTip: Serve over salad or cauliflower rice.

title: Hummus Veggie Snack Plate

steps.text: Arrange hummus, vegetables, pita, and olives on a plate or lunch container.

storageNotes: Cut vegetables keep 3 days refrigerated.
prepAheadNotes: Portion hummus and vegetables into containers for quick snacks.
toddlerTip: Use soft pita strips and thin cucumber slices.
glucoseTip: Use more vegetables and fewer pita wedges.

title: Mediterranean Yogurt Parfait

steps.text: Spoon yogurt into a bowl and top with berries, walnuts, honey, and cinnamon.

storageNotes: Best assembled fresh; pre-portion toppings separately.
prepAheadNotes: Wash berries and portion nuts ahead.
toddlerTip: Skip whole nuts for young toddlers; use ground nuts or seed butter if appropriate.
glucoseTip: Use minimal honey and add extra walnuts for satiety.

title: Turkey Stuffed Peppers with Feta

steps.text: Brown turkey in a skillet with garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Stir in quinoa, tomatoes, spinach, and half the feta.
Fill pepper halves, top with remaining feta, and bake at 375°F until peppers are tender.

storageNotes: Keeps 4 days refrigerated.
reheatNotes: Microwave or bake covered until warmed through.
prepAheadNotes: Assemble peppers up to 24 hours before baking.
toddlerTip: Chop cooked pepper and filling into bite-size pieces.
glucoseTip: Use less quinoa and more spinach in the filling.

title: Herby Cottage Cheese Cucumber Toasts

steps.text: Toast bread until crisp.
Stir cottage cheese with dill, lemon juice, pepper, and a pinch of salt.
Spread cottage cheese on toast and top with cucumber and seasoning.

storageNotes: Best assembled fresh; cottage cheese mixture keeps 2 days.
reheatNotes: Toast bread fresh before serving.
prepAheadNotes: Mix the herbed cottage cheese and slice cucumber the night before.
toddlerTip: Cut toast into strips or serve cottage cheese and cucumber separately.
glucoseTip: Use one slice of toast and add extra cucumber or tomato.

title: Tomato Cucumber Farro Salad with Feta

steps.text: Cook farro according to package directions, then cool slightly.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Toss farro with tomatoes, cucumber, parsley, feta, and dressing.

storageNotes: Keeps 4 days refrigerated.
prepAheadNotes: Cook farro and chop vegetables ahead; toss with dressing before packing.
toddlerTip: Serve farro, cucumber, and feta in small separate piles.
glucoseTip: Add grilled chicken or chickpeas and keep farro to a smaller portion.

title: Turkey Spinach Meatballs with Orzo

steps.text: Mix turkey, spinach, egg, breadcrumbs, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Shape into meatballs and bake at 425°F until cooked through, about 18 minutes.
Cook orzo and serve with meatballs and lemon yogurt sauce.

storageNotes: Meatballs and orzo keep 4 days refrigerated.
reheatNotes: Reheat meatballs and orzo; add yogurt sauce after warming.
prepAheadNotes: Shape meatballs up to a day ahead or freeze uncooked on a tray.
toddlerTip: Cut meatballs into quarters and serve sauce for dipping.
glucoseTip: Swap half the orzo for roasted zucchini or salad.

title: Shrimp Zucchini Skillet with Tomatoes

steps.text: Sauté zucchini in olive oil until lightly browned.
Add garlic and tomatoes; cook until tomatoes soften.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, then finish with basil and feta.

storageNotes: Best within 2 days refrigerated.
reheatNotes: Reheat gently to avoid tough shrimp.
prepAheadNotes: Slice zucchini and tomatoes ahead; cook shrimp right before serving.
toddlerTip: Chop shrimp finely and serve zucchini soft.
glucoseTip: Serve as-is or over cauliflower rice for a lower-carb dinner.

title: Roasted Red Pepper Hummus Turkey Wraps

steps.text: Spread hummus over each tortilla.
Layer turkey, romaine, cucumber, and roasted red peppers.
Roll tightly and slice in half for lunch boxes.

storageNotes: Wraps keep 1 day; pack tightly to prevent drying.
prepAheadNotes: Slice vegetables and portion hummus ahead; assemble the morning of eating.
toddlerTip: Make pinwheels or serve turkey and vegetables deconstructed.
glucoseTip: Use a low-carb tortilla or make lettuce wraps with extra turkey.

title: Date-Tahini Overnight Oats

steps.text: Whisk yogurt, milk, tahini, chia seeds, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Stir in oats and chopped dates, then divide among jars.
Refrigerate overnight; loosen with a splash of milk before serving.

storageNotes: Keeps refrigerated up to 4 days.
reheatNotes: Serve cold or gently warm with extra milk.
prepAheadNotes: Assemble jars on prep day for grab-and-go breakfasts.
toddlerTip: Chop dates very small and thin with extra milk for younger toddlers.
glucoseTip: Top with walnuts and keep dates modest for steadier carbs.

title: Spinach Feta Egg Muffins

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk eggs with dill, oregano, salt, and pepper; fold in spinach, feta, and roasted peppers.
Divide into muffin cups and bake 16–18 minutes until just set.

storageNotes: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months.
reheatNotes: Microwave 20–30 seconds from fridge or thaw overnight from frozen.
prepAheadNotes: Bake on prep day for quick breakfasts or snack boxes.
toddlerTip: Cut into strips and serve with fruit.
glucoseTip: Pair with berries or cucumber instead of toast for a lower-carb plate.

title: Labneh Berry Toasts

steps.text: Toast bread until sturdy and lightly crisp.
Spread each slice with labneh and scatter blueberries over the top.
Finish with pistachios, lemon zest, and a very light honey drizzle.

storageNotes: Best assembled fresh; keep labneh and toppings separate.
reheatNotes: Toast bread fresh before assembling.
prepAheadNotes: Wash berries and chop pistachios ahead.
toddlerTip: Skip honey for children under 12 months; cut toast into fingers.
glucoseTip: Use one slice plus extra labneh and berries for a smaller carb portion.

title: Cucumber Hummus Snack Plates

steps.text: Spoon hummus into small bowls and dust with zaatar.
Arrange cucumber spears, carrots, pita triangles, and feta around the hummus.
Pack in divided containers if using for lunch boxes.

storageNotes: Pack vegetables and pita separately from hummus up to 3 days.
reheatNotes: No reheating needed.
prepAheadNotes: Slice cucumbers and portion hummus on prep day.
toddlerTip: Use soft pita strips and thin cucumber half-moons for easier biting.
glucoseTip: Lean into vegetables and feta; use fewer pita triangles.

title: Apricot Pistachio Yogurt Cups

steps.text: Divide Greek yogurt among four cups.
Top with chopped apricots, pistachios, cinnamon, and orange zest.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate for snack boxes.

storageNotes: Keeps covered up to 3 days; pistachios soften slightly.
reheatNotes: Serve chilled.
prepAheadNotes: Chop apricots and pistachios ahead, or assemble cups fully.
toddlerTip: Finely mince apricots and pistachios or swap nuts for seed butter swirl if needed.
glucoseTip: Use fewer apricots and extra pistachios for a lower-sugar cup.

title: White Bean Rosemary Crostini

steps.text: Blend beans, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, rosemary, salt, and pepper until mostly smooth.
Toast baguette slices until crisp on the edges.
Spread bean mash on toast and finish with a tiny drizzle of olive oil.

storageNotes: Bean spread keeps refrigerated up to 4 days; toast bread fresh.
reheatNotes: Toast bread before serving; bean spread can be served cool or room temperature.
prepAheadNotes: Make the bean spread on prep day for fast snacks or lunches.
toddlerTip: Serve bean spread as a dip with soft pita instead of crisp toast.
glucoseTip: Use cucumber rounds as dippers instead of some toast slices.

title: Lemon Oregano Cod with Tomato Olive Relish

steps.text: Heat oven to 400°F. Rub cod with 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Bake cod on a sheet pan for 10–12 minutes until it flakes easily with a fork.
Stir tomatoes, olives, parsley, lemon juice, and remaining olive oil into a quick relish.
Serve cod over warm couscous with tomato olive relish spooned on top.

storageNotes: Cooked cod is best within 2 days; relish keeps 3 days separately.
reheatNotes: Reheat cod gently at low power or serve room temperature over warm couscous.
prepAheadNotes: Chop relish vegetables and cook couscous up to 2 days ahead.
toddlerTip: Flake fish carefully and serve relish on the side for dipping or skipping.
glucoseTip: Serve over cauliflower rice or extra cucumber salad instead of some couscous.

title: Moroccan Chickpea Sweet Potato Stew

steps.text: Warm olive oil in a Dutch oven. Sauté onion 5 minutes until soft, then bloom garlic, cumin, paprika, and cinnamon for 30 seconds.
Add sweet potatoes, chickpeas, tomatoes, broth, salt, and pepper. Simmer 18–22 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Fold in spinach until wilted and adjust seasoning with a squeeze of lemon if available.
Serve in bowls with a spoonful of Greek yogurt for creaminess.

storageNotes: Keeps refrigerated up to 4 days and freezes well without yogurt.
reheatNotes: Reheat in a saucepan with a splash of broth or water.
prepAheadNotes: Dice onion and sweet potatoes ahead; stew can be fully batch-cooked.
toddlerTip: Mash sweet potatoes slightly and serve yogurt stirred in to mellow the spices.
glucoseTip: Use extra spinach and a smaller sweet potato portion; add chicken if more protein is needed.

title: Herby Lemon Tahini Sauce

steps.text: Whisk tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and a pinch of salt until thick and pale.
Slowly whisk in water until the sauce turns smooth and drizzleable.
Fold in parsley and dill, then taste for lemon and salt.

storageNotes: Keeps refrigerated in a jar for 5 days; thickens as it chills.
reheatNotes: No reheating needed; loosen with warm water before serving.
prepAheadNotes: Make on prep day to use on bowls, wraps, roasted vegetables, and snack plates.
toddlerTip: Serve as a dip in a small cup; thin with yogurt for a milder flavor if desired.
glucoseTip: Use as a high-fat sauce to make vegetable-heavy bowls more satisfying without adding sugar.

title: Cinnamon Fig Overnight Oats

steps.text: Stir oats, Greek yogurt, milk, chia seeds, cinnamon, orange zest, and a small pinch of salt in a mixing bowl until evenly combined.
Fold in chopped figs so they hydrate overnight and sweeten the oats naturally.
Divide into jars, cover, and refrigerate at least 8 hours or up to 4 days.
Top each jar with sliced almonds just before serving for crunch.

storageNotes: Keeps refrigerated in sealed jars up to 4 days.
reheatNotes: Eat cold or warm gently in the microwave with an extra splash of milk.
prepAheadNotes: Batch on Sunday night for grab-and-go breakfasts through midweek.
toddlerTip: Chop figs very small and soften with an extra splash of milk for younger toddlers.
glucoseTip: Pair with extra Greek yogurt or a boiled egg if you want more protein and a slower morning rise.

title: Lemon Oregano Salmon Tray Bake

steps.text: Toss potatoes with half the olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper; roast at 425°F for 15 minutes.
Add salmon and green beans to the sheet pan, then drizzle with remaining olive oil, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Roast until salmon flakes easily and potatoes are tender, about 12 to 15 minutes.

storageNotes: Store salmon and vegetables together up to 3 days refrigerated.
reheatNotes: Reheat gently at 300°F or serve salmon chilled over greens.
prepAheadNotes: Halve potatoes and trim green beans up to 2 days ahead.
toddlerTip: Flake salmon carefully and serve with soft potato pieces.
glucoseTip: Use extra green beans and a smaller potato portion.

title: Turkey White Bean Skillet

steps.text: Brown turkey in a large skillet with olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Stir in beans and crushed tomatoes; simmer until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.
Fold in spinach until wilted and finish with parmesan if using.

storageNotes: Keeps up to 4 days and freezes well in single portions.
reheatNotes: Reheat on the stove or microwave with a splash of water.
prepAheadNotes: Rinse beans and mince garlic ahead for a 20-minute cook.
toddlerTip: Mash beans slightly and serve with toast strips.
glucoseTip: Serve over sautéed greens or cauliflower rice instead of bread.

title: Cucumber Feta Snack Plates

steps.text: Arrange cucumber, feta, pita wedges, hummus, and grapes on plates or lunch containers.
Keep hummus covered until ready to serve.

storageNotes: Pack components separately up to 2 days so pita stays dry.
reheatNotes: No reheating needed.
prepAheadNotes: Slice cucumbers and cube feta the night before.
toddlerTip: Cut grapes lengthwise and crumble feta for easier bites.
glucoseTip: Use more cucumber and feta with fewer pita wedges.

title: Herby Lentil Stuffed Peppers

steps.text: Place pepper halves in a baking dish and season lightly with salt.
Mix lentils, rice, tomato sauce, parsley, olive oil, and pepper in a skillet until warm.
Fill peppers with the lentil mixture, top with mozzarella if using, and bake at 400°F until peppers are tender, about 25 minutes.

storageNotes: Refrigerate stuffed peppers up to 4 days.
reheatNotes: Reheat covered at 350°F or microwave until hot.
prepAheadNotes: Cook lentils and rice ahead; assemble peppers the morning of baking.
toddlerTip: Chop the baked pepper and filling into small pieces.
glucoseTip: Use extra lentils and halve the rice if desired.

title: Za'atar Egg Breakfast Pitas

steps.text: Whisk eggs with za'atar, salt, and pepper.
Scramble eggs in a lightly oiled skillet until just set, about 4 minutes.
Spread yogurt inside warm pitas and fill with eggs, cucumber, and tomatoes.

storageNotes: Best fresh; refrigerate leftover eggs up to 3 days.
reheatNotes: Reheat eggs gently and assemble pitas after warming.
prepAheadNotes: Slice vegetables and portion yogurt the night before.
toddlerTip: Serve pita, eggs, and vegetables separately with a small yogurt dip.
glucoseTip: Use half a pita and add extra cucumber and tomato.

title: White Bean Tuna Cucumber Boats

steps.text: Scoop a shallow channel from each cucumber half to make boats.
Mix tuna, white beans, celery, lemon juice, olive oil, capers, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the tuna-bean mixture into cucumber boats and serve chilled.

storageNotes: Store filling and cucumber separately up to 2 days.
reheatNotes: No reheating needed.
prepAheadNotes: Make the filling ahead; fill cucumber boats right before eating.
toddlerTip: Serve as small cucumber rounds with tuna-bean salad on the side.
glucoseTip: This is naturally lower carb; add extra cucumber or greens if still hungry.

title: Moroccan Chickpea Couscous Skillet

steps.text: Sauté zucchini and carrot with olive oil, ras el hanout, salt, and pepper until softened.
Add chickpeas, diced tomatoes, and 1 cup water; simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in couscous, cover, remove from heat, and let stand until fluffy, about 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and finish with parsley.

storageNotes: Refrigerate up to 4 days.
reheatNotes: Reheat with a splash of water to loosen the couscous.
prepAheadNotes: Dice zucchini and shred carrot ahead for a fast weeknight skillet.
toddlerTip: Mash some chickpeas and serve with plain yogurt if spices are strong.
glucoseTip: Use extra zucchini and chickpeas with a smaller couscous portion.

title: Herbed Turkey Kofta Lettuce Plates

steps.text: Mix turkey, parsley, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper; shape into small oval kofta.
Bake on a sheet pan at 425°F until cooked through, about 16 minutes.
Serve kofta with lettuce leaves, tzatziki, and pita if using.

storageNotes: Refrigerate cooked kofta up to 4 days.
reheatNotes: Reheat kofta in a skillet or microwave; keep lettuce cold.
prepAheadNotes: Shape kofta up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate covered.
toddlerTip: Cut kofta into small strips and offer tzatziki as a dip.
glucoseTip: Build lettuce plates first and use pita as an optional side.
